tool_args.rationale: The observed response is monotone-concave over u_now, while the pilot signatures indicate a sink-gradient effect. Since s_grad is essentially fixed across all five paid rows, gradient inhibition and open-branch contributions are not identifiable. The targeted open-branch probe is the least-cost discriminating measurement.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the 2-layer sink-inhibited saturating siphon model
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All five pilot rows hold s_grad near 1, so they cannot identify sink inhibition strength or resolve the open branch term.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit cooperative Hill-2 or barrier-modulated siphon
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Both require meaningful s_grad variation; the archive specifically calls for an open-branch probe when its span is below 0.08.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a static quadratic or Michaelis-Menten curve
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The observed monotone concave response could fit these, but they ignore the observed sink-gradient signature.
The pilot has no evidence of memory dynamics, and this expensive batch is specified for identifying the coupled memory ODE.
